Roscón de Reyes

Served at: Immaculada

Serves 8-10Prep 30 minCook 1 hr 30 min

Roscón de Reyes is a traditional Spanish sweet bread enjoyed during the Immaculada and Epiphany celebrations. This festive ring-shaped cake is decorated with candied fruits and often contains a hidden figurine and a bean, symbolizing luck and misfortune for those who find them.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup whole milk (240 ml), warm
  • 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast (1 packet)
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar (100 g)
  • 4 cups all-purpose flour (480 g), plus extra for dusting
  • 1/2 tsp salt
  • 3 large eggs
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter (113 g), softened
  • 1 tbsp orange blossom water
  • Zest of 1 orange
  • Zest of 1 lemon
  • 1/4 cup candied orange peel (40 g), chopped
  • 1/4 cup candied cherries (40 g), halved
  • Powdered sugar, for dusting
  • 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash)
  • Optional: small figurine and dry bean for hiding inside

Method

  1. In a small bowl, combine warm milk and yeast; let sit for 10 minutes until frothy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together sugar, flour, and salt.
  3. Add eggs, softened butter, orange blossom water, orange zest, and lemon zest to the dry ingredients.
  4. Pour in the yeast mixture and knead the dough until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes by hand or 5 minutes with a stand mixer.
  5. Incorporate the chopped candied orange peel and cherries into the dough.
  6. Shape the dough into a ball and place it in a greased bowl; cover with a clean cloth and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
  7. Punch down the dough and form it into a large ring on a parchment-lined baking sheet, making a hole in the center.
  8. If desired, hide the figurine and bean inside the dough ring at this stage.
  9. Cover the ring and let it rise for another 30 minutes.
  10. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  11. Brush the dough ring with beaten egg and decorate the top with additional candied fruits.
  12. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown and cooked through.
  13. Remove from oven and let cool on a wire rack.
  14. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, substitute half the milk with cream.
  • If orange blossom water is unavailable, use vanilla extract as a substitute.
  • Serve with hot chocolate or coffee for a traditional festive treat.
